newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama passes measure to protect canal.
newsitem.headline: Panama passes measure to protect canal.

text.p: Panama's Congress has approved a plan to protect the Panama Canal's watershed and promote development projects on areas to be vacated by the United States in 1999, a government spokeswoman said on Thursday.

The measure, passed unanimously late on Wednesday, protects the canal's 805,000-acre (330,000-hectare) watershed from overdevelopment, she said. It is expected to be passed into law by President Ernesto Perez Balladares later this month.

Called the General and Regional Plan of the Reverted Areas, the plan also eliminates bureaucratic procedures for the Regional Interoceanic Authority (ARI), an independent body in charge of attracting investment for properties to be vacated by the U.S. within three years, an ARI spokeswoman said.
The United States will hand over control of the Panama Canal and withdraw all troops by Dec. 31, 1999, in accordance with bilateral treaties.
ARI promotes tourism, real estate and industrial projects on more than 70,000 acres (28,350 hectares) valued at some $4.61 billion.
